text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.6% today as tight global diesel markets and heating oil supply concerns continued to support refiner margins. The company has climbed 13% over two weeks as diesel and heating oil prices have spiked—a direct tailwind for refiners, since they profit from the spread between the crude oil they buy and the refined products they sell. Today's move reflects ongoing anxiety about diesel supply: the Northeast is bracing for winter heating oil bills up 21%, and geopolitical tensions (Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iranian tanker threats in the Strait of Hormuz) are keeping global crude prices elevated while diesel stockpiles remain tight.

Refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, which limits how much additional supply can be brought online to ease the shortage. The combination of strong product demand, constrained production, and supply-chain risks from the Middle East creates a favorable environment for refiners' profitability in the near term—though it also means consumers and businesses relying on diesel and heating oil are facing genuine cost pressures heading into winter.
